questions.q: What does the story of Kafka and the crying girl illustrate?
a: Love and loss are inseparable, and love returns in new forms
Grief fades fastest when it is ignored
Children understand loss better than adults do
Stories can replace the things we have lost
questions.why: The note hidden in the doll says that everything you love will be lost, but love returns differently.

questions.q: What happens if you try to avoid only the painful half of your emotions?
a: You end up suppressing your feelings altogether
You strengthen the positive feelings instead
You become more resilient over time
You feel the negative ones less intensely
questions.why: The summary says feelings live on spectrums, so rejecting one side means rejecting both.

questions.q: What does the cellist who played in besieged Sarajevo demonstrate?
a: Beauty and suffering can be impossible to separate
Music can restore order in a broken city
Artists should stay neutral during a war
Grief is best expressed through classical music
questions.why: Cain uses the scene to show that joy and pain often arrive together.

questions.q: Where does Cain trace America's habit of forced positivity?
a: To Calvinist settlers who believed everything was preordained
To the self-help industry of the 1980s
To frontier communities that needed optimism
To the rise of social media influencers
questions.why: With little control over their fate, settlers were encouraged to act like winners.

questions.q: Why does a heightened awareness of mortality make older people happier?
a: They appreciate good moments more and forgive more easily
They have fewer daily responsibilities to worry about
They gradually forget the losses they have suffered
They spend more time surrounded by family
questions.why: The summary says older people are slow to anger and quick to feel grateful.
